description: Pinned results for a run with more than one pipeline stage and no virtual pipeline stages (Megatron's non-interleaved one-forward-one-backward schedule). They are derived from an independent replay of Megatron's schedule order, not from upstream: DynamicUSP has no such order. 'orders' lists, per pipeline stage, the forward (F) and backward (B) microbatches in the order of the three loops of forward_backward_pipelining_without_interleaving (megatron/core/pipeline_parallel/schedules.py): min(stages - stage - 1, microbatches) warm-up forwards, then one forward and one backward in turn, then the backwards that are left. 'step_time' holds the step time of that order on given group times: 'rows' lists the CP groups of every microbatch as [first rank, ranks, forward ms, backward ms] of the whole model; an operation takes the time of its group divided by the stages, starts when the previous operation of its stage and the operation that produces its input have ended, and starts at the same time on all ranks of a group; 'per_mb_overhead_ms' is added once per microbatch. The values were computed by a standard-library replay that keeps the times per CP group and walks every stage on its own; the runtime scheduler keeps them per rank and walks one merged order, and must reproduce them bit for bit.

plans.description: Whole plans of the unmodified DynamicUSP solver at the commit of dcp_usp_frozen_plans.json (solve_gbs with pp_multiple = 1, Stage 1 only, the packaged profile), whose step-time objective was given this order in place of its interleaved plan, in the harness process only. 'candidates' are the counts of the search, with the Stage 1 layout of each count (the CP groups of every microbatch as [first rank, ranks, sample ids]) and its objective (the runtime adds the iteration tail of the cost model), or the reason why a count has no layout. 'stage2', where present, is the result with Stage 2 switched on: the outcome of every microbatch of the chosen count, the objective before and after, and the final layout.
